title: Woven baby blanket on a four-shaft loom
subtitle: A soft, balanced twill blanket in superwash merino, about 80 cm by 100 cm
excerpt: A four-shaft twill baby blanket in superwash merino produces a soft, drapey fabric that washes well and retains its structure. The blanket is about 80 cm wide and 100 cm long finished. The 2/2 twill structure gives a diagonal rib that is soft and flexible.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from traditional four-shaft twill weaving practice. Baby blankets in handwoven merino twill are a standard intermediate project in UK weaving guilds; the pattern is adapted from standard four-shaft twill drafts.

glossaryTerms.definition: A weave structure that produces a diagonal rib pattern by advancing the shed sequence by one shaft on each successive pick.
The number of warp ends per centimetre (or inch). The sett for this blanket is 7 to 8 ends per cm for 2/2 twill in fingering-weight merino.
The lengthwise threads on a loom, under tension during weaving.
The crosswise thread that builds the cloth by passing through the shed.

items.name: Superwash merino fingering-weight yarn for warp and weft
Four-shaft floor loom with at least 85 cm weaving width

content.text: At 8 ends per cm and 82 cm weaving width (allowing for 10 per cent draw-in to reach 80 cm finished width), the warp requires 656 threads. The loom waste and fringe allowance needs about 40 cm at each end; wind 180 cm of warp to produce a finished blanket of about 100 cm after finishing. Two 2/2 threads per dent in an 8-dent reed achieves the 8 epc sett cleanly.

For a balanced twill, the weft picks per centimetre should match the ends per centimetre. Check every 10 cm with a ruler or beat counter. A balanced 2/2 twill has the diagonal rib sitting at 45 degrees: if the rib is steeper, the picks per centimetre are too many; if shallower, too few.

Hemstitch both ends before cutting off. Machine wash the finished blanket on a wool cycle at 30°C in a mesh bag. The fabric will shrink about 10 per cent and soften noticeably after the first wash. Press lightly with a damp cloth while still slightly damp to even the surface. Trim and knot the warp fringe at each end.

items.problem: The twill diagonal changes direction midway through the piece
items.cause: A threading error in the repeat, or a treadling error that skipped or doubled a treadle
items.fix: Check the threading at the reversal point thread by thread. In a straight twill, threads pass through shafts 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 3, 4 in sequence with no breaks.

items.problem: The blanket has a weft-faced stripe across its width
items.cause: The beat became heavier for a row or two, packing more weft into the cloth and creating a visible horizontal band
items.fix: Maintain a consistent beat throughout. Mark a consistent beat pace before you start and check it periodically against the warp-per-centimetre reference.
